**MOTH Chess 2.0 — Evolution.** This release adds MOTH Engine, an original chess engine written in C++ and compiled to WebAssembly, with a trained evaluation network, three playing styles, offline play, automatic on-board suggestions on analysis boards, and a learning pipeline that promotes new models only on measured improvement. Stockfish 17.1 remains as a separate engine you can switch to. Everything runs locally.

## Install / upgrade in Brave
1. Download `moth-chess-v2.0.zip` below and unzip it.
2. In `brave://extensions` (Developer mode on), either click **Load unpacked** and choose `moth-chess-dist`, or press reload on your existing MOTH Chess entry after replacing the folder. Your settings and Memory are kept, and the database migrates automatically to schema v3.
3. New sections on the board page: **Play MOTH** and **MOTH Engine**.
4. To get suggestions on Lichess or Chess.com analysis boards: MOTH icon → **Allow on …**. After that, boards are recognised automatically.

## What's new
- **MOTH Engine.** Perft-verified legal move generation; iterative deepening with aspiration windows, PVS, quiescence search, transposition table, Zobrist hashing, null-move pruning and LMR, killer/history ordering, SEE, mate-distance scoring and MultiPV. Speaks UCI in its own Web Worker.
- **Evaluation.** A classical evaluation plus a trained NNUE-style residual network (768 → 2×64 → 1). The active model `moth-nn-2.0.4` measured **+22.6 ± 29.9 Elo** against the classical evaluation over 400 games (LOS 93%).
- **Aggressive / Balanced / Defensive** styles share one search and one network. They change choices between close moves (32–35% of middlegame positions), never forced wins: all three found 57/57 mates.
- **Opening book** with 6,606 positions and 10,189 moves, each validated by Stockfish, including 1,017 gambit moves, 14 traps and 161 tagged opening mistakes with refutations. Popularity never outranks soundness.
- **Fast answers.** Book → cache → time-managed search. Cached replies take about 0.07 ms, median searches 26–47 ms, and every search answers within the 100 ms deadline (worst observed 98 ms).
- **Play MOTH.** Offline games as either colour with seven levels, clocks, takebacks, resign, save and review, plus pondering on your time.
- **Learning.** 24,000 Lichess games (CC0) labelled by Stockfish, self-play, off-distribution augmentation, quiet-position filtering, versioned models, rollback, and a three-part promotion gate (validation loss, 400-game match, tactics). Five candidates so far: one approved, four rejected and kept on record. The in-browser **Learning Lab** runs the same pipeline on your own games.
- **Personal adaptation** from your games against MOTH: prepared opening lines and Coach advice, kept separate from the engine model. You can switch it off or delete the history.
- **On-board suggestions.** Automatic board recognition, with positions **verified** from the page's FEN or its legally replayed move list. Arrows, square highlights and an evaluation bar are drawn on the site's board in both orientations and follow resize and scroll. Lichess studies are now supported.

## Measured (Node/WASM, 2-core build machine)
- Tactics at 100 ms per puzzle: MOTH **225/235**, Stockfish 17.1 lite 235/235.
- Strength: about **2705 (2590–2815)** on Stockfish's own UCI_Elo scale, from 112 games at 50 ms/move. This is a rough scale, not FIDE.
- Tests: perft (6 reference positions), **174** unit tests and **27** Chromium browser tests, all passing in CI.

## Fair play
Suggestions appear only on analysis, study and practice boards you've allowed. Live, rated, TV, tournament and rated-puzzle pages are blocked by URL and by clock detection. Uncertain positions stay unverified until you confirm them. Pondering is used only in MOTH's own games. MOTH never moves pieces on a website.

## Known limitations
- Stockfish is clearly stronger.
- The 95th/99th latency percentiles of complex positions sit at the deadline.
- The network is small.
- Site adapters were tested against stand-in pages, not the live sites.
- Brave was not tested directly; testing used Chromium.
